questions.answer: I was more of a spare of the moment - and I wanted to better my English and UofT were a good English speaking University for sociology

questions.answer: very

questions.answer: be active at social groups

questions.answer: superficial talk, but it were nice that they engaged for when you were with them

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the openness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) the library is nice, but use the cafes around town - so much more cute and people talk in the library anyhow.
2) get a good balance - studying can get done a lot quicker than I realized so I had a lot of social time (since the assignments are much shorter than at UCPH)
3) I don't know - find housing close to the campus (I walked sometimes 3,5k to school)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: you can rent a bike for free (100$ deposite you do get back) 2 weeks use, 1 week break (BikeChain)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social life - I had a smiley feeling the entire time

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: speaking in English with people that is native in it (though my English is good it were still challenging)

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
